name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3{x}^{3}\sqrt{y},\,y(0)=4
$$

Using the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step. Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current values $x$ and $y?$

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=3x3y,y(0)=4 Using the trapezoidal method with step size Δx=0.5, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the general form of g(ynew) in terms of the new values xnew and ynew, and the current values x and y?

a
g(ynew)=ynew−34(xnew)3ynew−y−34(xnew)3y
b
g(ynew)=ynew−34(xnew)3ynew−y−34x3y
c
g(ynew)=ynew−34(xnew)3ynew−y−34x3y
d
g(ynew)=ynew−32(xnew)3ynew−y−32x3y
e
g(ynew)=ynew+34(xnew)3ynew−y−34x3y
